scope: Original hypothetical calculation exercises. Sources verify underlying definitions and economic principles; they are not sources of current numerical observations or tax schedules. Linear markets, Cournot behavior, fixed price multipliers, fixed baskets, Solow production, and simple random sampling are explicit teaching assumptions, not claims that real economies or official statistics use every simplified model.

sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.title: Scope and Sequence for Economic Content
sources.principlesVerified: Scarcity, opportunity cost, resource allocation, production, and comparative advantage based on lower opportunity cost. Numerical production functions and incremental cost examples are original applications.

sources.title: The PPF: Increasing Opportunity Cost
sources.principlesVerified: Moving along a production frontier entails a tradeoff, and the opportunity cost of an incremental change is the forgone production over that segment.

sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.title: Price Elasticity of Demand Explained
sources.principlesVerified: Demand elasticity measures relative quantity response to a price change. The exercises explicitly specify midpoint calculations or supplied percentage changes so denominators are unambiguous.

sources.title: A widget example of the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index
sources.principlesVerified: HHI sums the squares of firms' market shares; percentage shares produce the 0-to-10,000 scale. No contemporary merger-review thresholds are used.

sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.title: Understanding Fiscal Policy, Michael T. Owyang
sources.principlesVerified: The simple expenditure model yields spending multiplier 1/(1-MPC), lump-sum tax multiplier -MPC/(1-MPC), and balanced-budget multiplier one. Government transfers are excluded from government purchases in GDP. Exercises state fixed prices, closed economy, and no crowding out.

sources.title: Consumer Price Index: Calculation
sources.principlesVerified: Price aggregation depends on expenditure or quantity weights. Official CPI construction uses multiple stages and formulas; the exercises specifically call their fixed-basket or fixed-base weighted indexes simplified examples.

sources.title: Consumer Price Index Frequently Asked Questions
sources.principlesVerified: Inflation uses the percentage change in the price index, and a change in index points differs from a percentage change. Index ratios support purchasing-power comparisons and rebasing.

sources.title: Concepts and Definitions: Current Population Survey
sources.principlesVerified: Labor force is employed plus unemployed. Unemployment divides by the labor force; participation and employment-population ratios use the civilian noninstitutional population age 16+. U-6 adds marginal attachment and involuntary part-time work with the appropriate expanded denominator.

sources.title: Office of Productivity and Technology: Concepts
sources.principlesVerified: Labor productivity compares real output with hours worked. Total factor productivity measures output growth beyond the contributions of measured inputs; the exercises supply their growth-accounting approximation explicitly.

sources.title: Common Trade Definitions
sources.principlesVerified: The trade balance is exports less imports. Positive balances are surpluses and negative balances are deficits. The exercises distinguish goods, services, and income accounts.

sources.title: International Transactions
sources.principlesVerified: International transactions accounts cover goods, services, income, and international transfers. Only these accounting categories are used; all exercise amounts are invented.

sources.title: The Expenditures Approach to Measuring GDP
sources.principlesVerified: GDP by expenditures is C + I + G + X - M; subtracting imports excludes foreign production already included in spending components.

sources.title: Gross Domestic Product Release: Additional Information
sources.principlesVerified: Real values remove price effects, while nominal values use current prices. Growth exercises identify whether quantities are real, aggregate, or per person.

sources.title: Understanding Standard Errors and Confidence Intervals
sources.principlesVerified: A confidence interval combines an estimate, standard error, and appropriate critical value. The exercises explicitly supply a normal 95% critical value and specify simple-random-sample assumptions where s/sqrt(n) is used; they do not apply that simplification to complex CPS survey estimates.

sources.title: Statistical Quality Standard E1: Analyzing Data
sources.principlesVerified: Statistical analysis should identify uncertainty and the confidence level used. Population versus sample denominators and conditional probability populations are specified directly in the exercises.
